application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Online Australia Awards Scholarships Information System (OASIS)
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on OASIS portal between February 1 and April 30; select Pakistan country profile.
step_by_step_workflow: 1. Register on OASIS online portal (opens February 1).
2. Complete application form and select up to 2 Australian university courses.
3. Write Development Impact Plan (Re-entry plan): Explain what practical project you will implement in Pakistan upon return.
4. Upload degree certificates, transcripts, proof of 2 years work experience, and valid IELTS/TOEFL report.
5. Upload 2 referee reports (1 academic, 1 professional) on official DFAT templates.
6. Submit online application before April 30 deadline.
7. Initial eligibility and compliance screening by Australia Awards Pakistan team.
8. Shortlisted candidates invited for in-person panel interview in Islamabad (July - August).
9. Provisional selection announced (September).
10. Complete pre-departure training and Australian visa processing (subclass 500) (October - December).
11. Depart for Australia for Introductory Academic Program (January/February).

application_process_roadmap.portal_system_name: Monash Graduate Research Admissions and Scholarship Portal (my.app)
application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register an account on the Monash Graduate Research portal and select the 'Admission and Scholarship' combined pathway.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Verify Minimum Entry Requirements (Monash H1 equivalence: 80%+ research thesis or bachelor degree).
Step 2: Find a Supervisor via Monash 'Find an Expert' or Faculty Research Supervisor Directory.
Step 3: Submit Faculty Expression of Interest (EOI) or email potential supervisor with CV, academic transcripts, and 2-page research concept note.
Step 4: Receive formal 'Invitation to Apply' from the relevant Monash Faculty Graduate Research office.
Step 5: Prepare required documentation (transcripts, degree certificates, grading scale, English test report, research proposal, CV, referee contact details).
Step 6: Lodge formal application via Monash online application portal selecting 'Combined Candidature and Scholarship Application'.
Step 7: Referees receive automated email prompts to submit confidential assessment reports online.
Step 8: Faculty and University Graduate Research Committee (GRC) rank applications in central competitive scoring round.
Step 9: Receive formal Offer Letter (Course Offer + Scholarship Award Letter with OSHC and stipend terms).
Step 10: Formally accept scholarship offer, receive Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), and lodge Australian Student Visa (Subclass 500).

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Find a supervisor via UTS Find a Supervisor portal, obtain their written endorsement, then create an account on the UTS HDR online application system and submit for both admission and scholarship.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1 (April - June): Search UTS Find a Supervisor portal; contact prospective faculty members with CV, academic transcripts, and draft research proposal.
Step 2 (June - July): Interview with prospective supervisor; obtain their formal agreement to supervise and written Pre-Assessment / Supervisor Support Letter.
Step 3 (July - August): Prepare full application dossier: refined 3-5 page research proposal, 2 academic referee reports, IELTS test report, and attested transcripts.
Step 4 (By 31 August): Submit formal online application via UTS portal, ticking the box for 'UTS International Research Scholarship / RTP'.
Step 5 (September - October): Faculty Higher Degree Committee reviews and scores applications on H1 equivalence and research output.
Step 6 (November - December): UTS Graduate Research School releases scholarship outcomes and issues unconditional offers and Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).
Step 7 (December - January): Apply for Australian Subclass 500 Student Visa via ImmiAccount; complete biometrics and medical exam in Pakistan.
Step 8 (February - March): Travel to Sydney, attend UTS HDR orientation, and commence research candidature.

Step 2: Obtain formal written supervisory endorsement from the Otago academic.
